Mosharraf Hossain Sarder, DAG with Shahida Begum, AAG and Khondaker Moderesh Elahi, Advocates----- For the Petitioner Defendant-Appellant 
M. Kamrul Hoque Siddique with AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, Advocates----- For the Opposite-Parties Plaintiff-Respondents.
parties:
President, Coronation Hall Committee and DC, Khulna ----- Petitioner Defendant-Appellant
Vs.
Executive Committee, Khulna and others ----- Opposite Parties Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
in respect of the property described in the schedule to the plaint. The basis for claiming title in the suit land, being 0.28 acres of land under CS Plot No.45/117 under CS Khatian No. 473/1 corresponding to SA Plot No. 169 under SA Khatian No.7 of Mouja Helatola, Police Station and District Khulna, is that the suit land was gifted by the then Hindu Jaminder in favour of the plaintiff at the request of some cultural minded people of the locality. In support of the plaintiffs case, it has examined four persons as witnesses. It has also adduced and proved certain documents before the trial Court which were marked as Exhibits-1 to 13. 

 3. The Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner contested in the suit by filing written statement, denying all material allegations made in the plaint and further asserting that the plaintiff is not at all owner of the suit land and that it is the defendant Coronation Hall Committee which is the owner of the suit land and, accordingly, name of the defendant has been recorded in CS as well as SA Khatian as owner and possessor of the suit land including the Coronation Hall and other establishments built on the suit land. The defendant is represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna by virtue of his office as the president of the said committee, which is the land lord of the suit property including the Coronation Hall, situated thereon and let out to the Society Cinema Hall on 23-1-1997 and again on 1-11-2003. The Society Cinema Hall has been using the Coronation Hall as tenant of the defendant and that 40% of the rental income would have been paid, as donation, to the plaintiff. The Executive Committee of the plaintiff was dissolved since the secretary of the plaintiff organization died and it was essential that a constitution of the plaintiff should be adopted, the income and expenditure statement of the plaintiff organization should be examined, so the Executive Committee of the plaintiff had to be dissolved. But, when account of the income and expenditure of the plaintiff was called for, the Secretary Mr. Enamul Haque Milu had failed to account for the income and expenditure of the plaintiff organization and he, apprehending probable prosecution, has filed this suit to plead as defence. The defendant has examined one witness to prove its case and has also adduced and proved certain documents before the trial Court, which were marked as Exhibits-Ka to Chao 

 8. Mr. Mosharraf Hossain Sarder, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the petitioner along with Mrs. Shahida Begum and Mr. Khondaker Moderesh Elahi, learned Assistant Attorneys General having placed the application for revision and drawn our attention to the materials on record, firstly submits that in this particular case the Court of appeal has not independently assessed the evidence on record for itself as the last Court of facts and without reading the evidence properly interpreting the evidence adduced in the case, has erroneously affirmed the judgment and the, decree passed by the Court below. Besides the appellate Court has also failed to appreciate and apply the principles of law decided by the Supreme Court and cited before him at the time of hearing argument. He next submits that, the trial Court although recorded that neither of the parties to the suit has been able to prove original title in the suit land and that the plaintiff has failed to prove the alleged gift made in their favour by the then zaminders. It has, however, decreed the suit without appreciating the settled legal position that the onus lie on the plaintiff to prove its case and that the plaintiff cannot succeed on basis of the weakness or lacuna in the defence case. He next submits that, the trial Court has passed the decree stating as reason that even if for arguments sake it is considered that the plaintiff has failed to prove the fact of acquiring title on the basis of any gift, then it has at least acquired title by virtue of adverse possession, whereas the settled law is that adverse possession cannot be the basis of claiming title, nor it was the case of the plaintiff that it has acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree has been passed erroneously as well as based on a third case, not to be found in the pleadings. He then submits that the Court below ought to have noticed that in the CS and SA Khatian (Exhibit Umma and Umma-1) name of the defendant has been recorded as owner as well as the land development tax receipt (খাজনা দাখিলা), Exhibit-4 series, also prove payment of Khazna in the name of the defendant. Exhibit-2 SA Khatian No. 7 and the Khazna Dhakila prove possession and ownership of the defendant in the suit land as well as in the establishments built there- upon. He also submits that the two agreements, marked as Exhibit-9 series, also proved that the Coronation Hall was let out to the Society Cinema Hall by the defendant as land lord. These evidences also proved title and ownership of the defendant in the suit properties, which both Courts below have failed to read, to interpret and to appreciate. Finally he submits that, the schedule of the plaint is vague and the suit property cannot be identified with reference to the schedule. Hence on this ground also the suit ought to have been dismissed. He concludes submitting that, the suit has been filed by the plaintiff in anticipation of litigation for their failure to render accounts as to the income and expenditure of the plaintiff organization which was receiving donation from the defendant at the rate of 40% of the rental income and the defendant had authority to ask for rendering accounts by the plaintiff organization. Accordingly, the learned Advocate maintained that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court has committed error of the law and that has resulted in error in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning failure of justice, so the impugned judgments and decrees are liable to be set-aside and the suit be dismissed. In support of his contentions the learned Deputy Attorney General has referred to that cases Abdul Kader vs Abdullah, reported in 51 DLR 435; Noor Mohammad Khan vs Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR 435; Kamal Baksh vs Siraj Bakshi, reported in 7 BLT (AD) 329 and Bangladesh vs Abdul Hye, reported in 56 DLR (AD) 53. 

 15. Having perused plaint, we find that the plaintiff has not claimed declaration of its title or ownership or possession in the suit properties based on any adverse possession. Rather, their specific case-was that, at the request of some dignitaries and cultural minded people of the locality the then Hindu Zaminder has gifted the property in favour of the plaintiff, but both the Court below have recorded that the plaintiff has failed to' prove any such gift made in its favour. Rather, the CS Khatian No. 473/1 (exhibit-uma) adduced by the defendant clearly proves that 16 annas of the suit land originally belonged to ভারত সম্রাট পক্ষে পাবলিক ওয়ার্কস ডিপার্টমেন্ট i.e. the government, not by Hindu Zaminders. This evidence on record repudiates the case that any Hindu Zaminder was owner of the suit property or that they could have made any gift in respect of the said property without a registered deed of gift and that both the Courts below have utterly failed to read this evidence and to appreciate that the CS Khatian No. 473/1 (exhibit-uma) proves that original title of the suit land lies in the government represented by the Department of Public Works, which is now under the Ministry of Public Works & Housing Settlement of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 The trial Court and the appellate Court both have failed to appreciate that the plaintiff cannot succeed on the basis of any lacuna or defect in the defence case. They have also failed to take into deliberation that there CS or RS Khatians were never challenged by the plaintiff. Rather, the plaintiff has proved and relied upon the RS Khalian No. 7 (exhibit uma-1 of the plaintiff) as well as the khajanadhakhila (exhibit-4 series) and the City Corporation holding tax receipts (exhibit-6 series), all of which proves continuous and uninterrupted possession on the defendant since the time of CS Record, the land being the khash land. 

 21. Looking at the documentary evidence, Exhibit-Umma and Umma-1 which are the CS Khatian No. 471/1 and the corresponding SA Khatian No.7 of Mouja Helatola, Police Station and District-Khulna, comprising CS Plot No. 45/117, corresponding to SA Plot No. 169, we find that these evidences clearly prove that 0.28 acres of land in the CS Khatian has been recorded in the name of the Government of India (ভারত সম্রাট) represented by its Public Works Department as the owner and name of the President Coronation Hall Committee has been recorded as the occupant of the sixteen annas of the suit land. In the corresponding SA Khatian No.7 name of President Coronation Hall Committee has been recorded for sixteen annas of the suit land, although in the CS Khatian the Coronation Hall Committee was a mere occupant or licensee as distinguished from a tenure-holder or Raiyat only to use the suit property for the specific purpose to observe the event of coronation by a committee formed to that end, namely-Coronation Hall Committee, Khulna. This factual position is also supported and corroborated by the SA Khatian No. 7 submitted and proved by the plaintiff itself and marked as Exhibit-2. The possession of Coronation Hall Committee in the suit land is further supported by Exhibit-4 series, which are the land development tax receipts from Bangla 1386 to 1408 and all in the name of defendant, submitted and proved by the plaintiff. All these rent receipts (খাজনা দাখিলা) are in the name of Coronation Hall Committee, Khulna. Besides, the City Corporation tax receipts in the name of the defendant, (exhibit 6 series) adduced and proved by the plaintiff, also support the defence case. As such the positive case of the defendant that the suit land as well as the properties thereon has been recorded in CS Khatian and in the RS Khatian are in the name of the defendant and that Khazana (land development tax) and the holding tax in respect of the suit properties are being paid by the defendant have been proved before the trial Court. But both the Courts below have found the plaintiff in possession, which is contrary to the documentary evidence on record and this clearly makes out the case of non-reading and misreading of evidence on record by the trial Court as well as by the appellate Court, as the last Court of fact. Hence, the findings, as to the title and possession, arrived at by the Courts below, are contrary to the evidence on record and are perverse, hence liable to be reversed. 

 Here we find that, the trial Court has arrived at this finding by totally brushing aside the C.S Khatian (exhibit-Uma), RS Khatian (exhibit-uma(1), khajanadhakhila (exhibit-4 series) and the Khulna City Corporation holding tax receipts (exhibit 6 series ) all showing the possession of Coronation Hall Committee in the suit properties. The trial Court has also ignored the fact that the plaintiffs was allowed to use the green room (সাজঘর) and the Coronation Hall by the Coronation Hall Committee and that such use was based on the consent or license of the Coronation Hall Committee. Besides the trial Court has also failed to appreciate that all the documentary evidence showing possession of the Coronation Hall Committee in the suit property, the possession of the plaintiff, even if they had any, would be mere unlawful possession which cannot be protected by a Court of law against the lawful owner, i.e. the defendant in this case. Besides, such finding is contrary to the law declared in 4 BLT (AD) (1996) 150; Md. Benzir Ahmed vs Debendra Chandra Saha, quoted above. 

 27. We have also noticed that, when the CS and SA Khatians and the khajanadhakila adduced and proved before the trial Court clearly prove the possession arid prima facie title of the defendant, the plaintiff has filed this suit for declaration simpliciter, without asking for consequential relief and without payment of advalorume Court fees, upon proper valuation of the suit. But the trial Court as well as the appellate Court have failed to appreciate this defect in the suit and have failed to find that the suit, as filed and valued, was not maintainable in its present form and was liable to be dismissed under the proviso to section 42 of the Special Relief Act, 1877 as well as for want of proper valuation and nonpayment of advalorume Court fees. 

 33. However, it is very much pertinent to record here that the CS Khatian (Exhibit-Umma) has been recorded in the name of Public Works Department representing the Government (ভারত সম্রাট) and name of Coronation Hall Committee has been recorded in the CS Khatian as a mere occupant for an specific purpose, i.e. to observe the event of coronation by forming a committee, not as a tenure-holder or as a raiyat. But in the corresponding SA Khatian No.7 (Exhibit-Umma-1 ) of the defendant, (which is Exhibit-2 of the plaintiff) name of President, Coronation Hall Committee, has been  recorded by omitting name of the government represented by Ministry of Public Works, although there is nothingon record to justify commission of the name of the government. As such, in the SA Khatian name of the owner of the suit property, being the Khash land has been committed and the illegally the RS Khatian is not correct, hence the same is needed to be corrected. This, having been noticed by us, we are of the view that, appropriate direction should be made to correct the SA Khatian and the subsequent Khatians in consonance with the concerned CS Khatian (Exhibit 'Uma') by recording the name of the government represented by the Ministry of Public Works, in khash khatian. 

 In the result, this rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. Judgment and decrees of both the Courts below are hereby set-aside and the Title Suit No. 49 of 2002 of the Court of Joint District Judge, Khulna is hereby dismissed. The Deputy Commissioner, Khulna is directed, in exercise of the power vested in this Court under section 151 and 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Article 101 and 109 of the Constitution, to get corrected the SA and the subsequent Khatians in connection with suit property and to record the suit property, in Khash Khatian, in the name of the government represented by the Ministry of Public Works. Concerned Assistant Commissioner Land and the Tahshil Office, Kanungo are directed to record the suit property in Khas Khatian, towards performance of their duty as per Article 112 of the Constitution. The suit property should be managed by the Coronation Hall Committee, Khulna in the manner as before, as a management body on behalf of the government, until otherwise decided by the government. Let, copies of this judgment be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Law to issue a circular in the light of the law declared by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 8 LG (2011) (AD) 70 for information and compliance of the learned Judges of the sub-ordinate Courts. Let copies of the judgment also be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works, Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh and to the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna for necessary steps for recording the suit property in Khash Khatian.
